warnings:
lineage agent notes: - n_claims is COUNT(*). No input column feeds its value, so I recorded it as coming from dw.claims_enriched.customer_id (a grouping key) at low confidence. The same applies to points, score and tier through n_claims.
- severity divides paid by MEAN(paid) without a GROUP BY. SAS fills that mean in across every row of each per-line table, so it is the average over that line's customers. PySpark needs a window over lob_code to match.
- Only lines MOT, HOM and TRV survive (lines 69 and 74). Rows match lob_code exactly; trailing blanks in char 5 are ignored when SAS compares strings.
- Both joins on lines 84–85 are LEFT joins, so they keep every row. They could still duplicate rows if dw.dim_customer has more than one row per customer_id. dim_customer has version_count and _row_seq, which suggests it may keep history. The scoring step does not dedup.
- loss_ratio comes from an inner join with rpt.premium_band_summary (line 55). A line with no premium rows gets a missing loss_ratio. That makes lob_points, points, score and tier missing too, and a missing score falls to tier 'LOW'.
- If date_of_birth is missing, age is missing and age_load is 1.00.
- The ORDER BY on line 86 only sorts the rows. It decides no row survival, so I recorded no ranks edges.
